shots.text: In a Delhi summer, shade decides whether a street can be walked. {GreenCityAI|GreenCity AI} finds the heat, street by street, and tests the fix before anyone builds it.

chapter: A digital twin from open data
shots.text: This is Connaught Place, New Delhi, as our own twin, built from open data, and on Google's photoreal {3D|3D} tiles, which are only for the view. The twin does the measuring: {212|two hundred and twelve} buildings from OpenStreetMap, {936|nine hundred and thirty-six} trees from a satellite canopy map on AWS, and the true sun for the {15th|fifteenth} of May.

Every hour, we trace the sun onto every footpath. At {7 a.m.,|seven a.m.,} a third of the walkways are in shade. By noon, the sun is {79|seventy-nine} degrees high, and only {4 percent|four percent} are. The hex map shows where walkers have nowhere to hide.
Around it, we read a kilometre of the city, and every number wears a label: observed, computed, simulated or proposed.

chapter: Simulated peak hour · Middle Circle × Radial Road 2
shots.text: In simulated peak traffic, {20|twenty} road links run over capacity, shown in red, the worst at {1.87|one point eight seven} times. Analyze scans Middle Circle at Radial Road {2:|two:} one approach carries {1.57|one point five seven} times its capacity, and at {3 p.m.,|three p.m.,} {85 percent|eighty-five percent} of the walkway nearby is in direct sun.
An AI doctor explains the problem. It answers only by calling our measuring tools, and a checker traces every number back to a tool.

Then we test fixes. Diverting some trips cuts the load from {1.57|one point five seven} to {1.44|one point four four} times capacity. {200|Two hundred} street trees lift day-long walkway shade from {13.9|thirteen point nine} to {17 percent.|seventeen percent.} Costs are labelled assumed, not quotes.
It works anywhere on Earth. Search for Marina Bay Sands in Singapore, and the city map appears at once. Press build, and in under two minutes, a new twin is ready.

Got a drone? Upload its point cloud, of any town or city. This public drone survey of the IIT Gandhinagar campus has {12.6 million|twelve point six million} points, and the file finds its own place on the map. The scan measures {71 of 73|seventy-one of seventy-three} buildings, and finds {2,380|two thousand three hundred and eighty} trees.
Every point here is real, shown as a photo, by class, or by height. Ground, roofs and trees are segmented from the point cloud by our own pipeline.
And the same scan as {3D|three-D} Gaussian splats: one splat for each measured point, drawn by our own WebGL renderer.
In New York, the same viewer reads public {USGS|USGS} airborne LiDAR, and draws the open-data twin as Gaussian splats too.
{GreenCityAI:|GreenCity AI:} open data and drone scans in, cooler streets out.
